title: Direct Field Method examples for photonics and plasmonics
description: Fortran programs and case inputs for the numerical examples of the tutorial Computational photonics and plasmonics: A direct physical approach, including the gap-graded surface meshes of the three-rod example and the Python script that generates them; a Python exercise; the numerical results and Python plotting scripts for Figs. 2, 3, 5 and 7; and a Python post-processing script that computes the fields and radar cross section of perfect conductors from the surface current of the magnetic-field solution, as used for the low-frequency case of Fig. 3. The Direct Field Method solves Maxwell's equations in the frequency domain directly for the Cartesian components of the electric and magnetic fields with non-singular boundary integral equations discretized by curved six-node quadratic triangular elements. Four programs cover perfectly conducting and dielectric scatterers, the spectra and surface-field gradients of eccentric Au-core/Ag-shell nanoparticles, and optical forces and torques; the exercise compares the computed surface field of a perfectly conducting sphere with Mie theory.
notes: Companion code to the article 'Computational photonics and plasmonics: A direct physical approach' by E. Klaseboer, D. Y. C. Chan, A. J. Yuffa, A. C. Yucel and Q. Sun, submitted to Journal of Physics: Photonics (2026).
